rv.q: What makes 'In the Heights' special is that Mr. Miranda has managed to write a musical that is simultaneously of the moment and timeless
But when In the Heights is at its best, the talented ensemble forges a genuine sense of community, and turns Broadway into a block party to remember.
Depth of feeling, together with the wit of Miranda’s lyrics, the playful dexterity of his rhymes, his dynamic score and a bunch of truly winning performances, make the show an uncalculated charmer.
The show is an exuberant celebration of Latino culture in Washington Heights, with a score that mixes hip-hop, salsa, merengue, and pop in ways that feel both contemporary and timeless.
If the tale seems scattered, you don't mind its lack of focus because the hardworking actors are so appealing.

This extraordinary show will be the most influential and important musical of the season.
Lack of power, however, is no way to describe In the Heights, which ignited a new energy source for musical theater last night at the Theatre.
But reality is not the issue here; rather, it is fantasy, music, singing and dancing, and some salty dialogue, as well as flawless production values and performance.
This exuberant musical about dreams deferred and realized in Washington Heights is a blast of fresh air that blows through the Theatre like a cool breeze on a hot summer day.
Meanwhile, with the deeply flawed and deeply pleasurable "In the Heights," this town just got a tiny bit more wonderful.
Miranda's score is short on the melodic punch that's a vital element of any memorable musical.
All the tweaking has turned the evening into an immensely satisfying experience that is sure to charm even the most entrenched cynic.
In the Heights has got a beat; it's got energy. But it's finally so much less than it ought to have been!
